title: GPT-6 Astra Just Dropped and Reviewers Already Cooking Insane AI Games
author: JoseQuanGT
selftext:
According to YT’s Mathew Berman GPT-6 is amazing at coding videogames… from Little Planet to a Sim City clone…

Wonderful time to be a builder/creator 😎

Will it dethrone Claude for AI game development???

Check Mathew Berman’s YT review just published

https://youtu.be/xdXLzFzxA9Q?si=L-BVhd45v\_rM-rIN

comments.author: Tayro2
comments.body: He talked so much about AI, now he sounds like one of

comments.author: pilipalipeli
comments.body: I can't wait to get excited over more slop!

replies.author: Diddlingdiddlerdiddy
replies.body: Why are you here?

replies.author: Flash1987
replies.body: Where is he wrong though, these one shot make a game shit are the worst of the slop. Its just a bunch of wasting tokens to make something semi playable and then abandoned.

replies.author: Maleficent_Pen_9076
replies.body:
Yeah, I am not impressed at all at AI generating some unplayable slop

I'll be impressed when it can generate relevant, helpful material into your world. Not saying that's far off, but not impressed yet.

comments.author: Initial-Theme-462
comments.body: Very excited to get home so I can try this out!!

comments.author: ZerkyXii
comments.body: New AI models are just like new call of dutys same shit more expensive

replies.author: nicktehbubble
replies.body: Except making the old shit literally worse

comments.author: yn3kk
comments.body: Had me going for a minute about a GTA 6 AI model that leaked, ngl

replies.author: JoseQuanGT
replies.body: Probably can ask it to search for the leaked files 🤔

replies.author: DisasterSpaghetti106
replies.body:
I can't wait for the era where full scale AAA games even with GTA7 graphics or so that will be generated by people who can use AIs like Maestros in an orchestra Whole new worlds to explore by countless game architects/designers who have brilliant ideas but are just not popular enough to make it to the "Hollywood" of video game industry. 

..only for them to be replaced by even more advanced AI-maestros.

The near-future is amazing, we already live in a magic era that if we could talk about it to our minus 10 year-old self they would call us lunatics.

comments.author: clayrender
comments.body: you can download an asset for free that accomplishes the same in the same amount of time...

replies.author: JoseQuanGT
replies.body: AI is known to cheat when it thinks its being tested, maybe that’s what it did… but it is still impressive in my opinion

replies.author: Council-Member-13
replies.body:
Still extremely impressive, but still, it's the one-shot experience. It will build something neat and cohesive, often by repurposing existing assets. But the moment you want to change, add, or refine something, it becomes a real slog.

I just added a flyout menu to my app and had to requery it like 10 times just to get the layering right. Obviously, this was with 5,6 on high, and maybe Astra is miles ahead. The DeepSWE benchmarking does certainly indicate that it is better at real/independent/non-cheaty coding.

comments.author: astrielx
comments.body: We have vastly different understandings of the word 'insane'

replies.author: JoseQuanGT
replies.body: Creating a Little Planet web game with a two sentence prompt… YES!!! its “insane good” or “insanely bad ai slop”, wont debate u, but having the technology its bonkers

replies.author: Annual_Manner_8654
replies.body: OP is another karma farmer, yawn, they post short clips of "insane" games. Who cares. Link me a playable one that someone has reviewed after actually playing it

comments.author: Salt-Willingness-513
comments.body: so how about the weekly limits? is it sipping as 5.6 sol does? honestly thats the only thing keeping me away from openai right now

replies.author: JoseQuanGT
replies.body: In my experience Claude is worst (5 prompts and several hours waiting for reset)… guess someone has to pay for the data center buildout 🫣

replies.author: Salt-Willingness-513
replies.body: i have same experience with both. Claude has the small 5h and weekly limit which is annoying and codex has the extremely small weekly limit (at least with pro 20 and 5.6 xhigh) and random resets to hope for. I just want to work undisturbed.

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
I kinda hate this type of content. It looks cool but it breaks my heart a little as a keen amateur. It is an asset flip on steroids.

It makes all the effort I am putting into slowly crafting my own game feel utterly pointless when anybody can just say “make me a game” and get it looking like this.

replies.author: JoseQuanGT
replies.body:
I think it pushes devs creators to do much more… maybe dedicate more into game asthetics, story, etc.

Embrace change, its the only sure thing going forward

replies.author: Psychological-Key-36
replies.body: No one will ever play this game and very little amount of people will actually play fully vibe coded games. 2 prompt games are basically a game within the AI itself for the user to just create games out of thin air, but the chances of AI outputting a successful steam game have to be pretty much zero. The gaming experience here is playing a game that you just prompted out of pocket

replies.author: Abracadabroo
replies.body: Yeah, I'm vibecoding a game right now (mostly to see for myself if its possible) and I think making something quality is actually quite a bit of work still. Even if it nails coding aspects, claude still doesn't know shit about what is actually **fun**. I have to get very granular and spend hours to days on game balancing prompts and back and forth to make sure I am getting what I want. Nobody is making a steam game with 10 minutes of prompting

replies.author: avigard
replies.body:
>very little amount of people will actually play fully vibe coded games

Will age like raw untreated milk on a hot summer day

replies.author: Financial_Alps3369
replies.body: Trust me, game design is the one part that still needs to be crafted by a human. Two-prompt games are very impressive graphically and mechanically, but they are rarely fun.

comments.author: Ianuarius
comments.body: Really diluting the definition of a "game" there.

replies.author: JoseQuanGT
replies.body:
If u watch the whole yt video, Astra made a fully functional Sim City clone

https://reddit.com/link/p7qoiya/video/19q3hvjcsgnh1/player

replies.author: Feeling_Coyote_513
replies.body: Its just three.js. a shiny 3d demo but nothing more. You are all fooled by this. Ask chatgpt and you see. Lol

comments.author: jellobend
comments.body:
When I look at this I immediately want to see an admin panel of sorts to manage the finer details of game logic.

I know I can use existing engines like Godot or Unity for this, nevertheless I think we need a new breed of game engines that are firendly with AI generated games. Probably some kind of standardization framework/protocol to anchor the AI's output as well, similar to MCP.

comments.author: Feeling_Coyote_513
comments.body: Most people are fooled by this. These are just made with three.js which sucks, and is not a game engine. He wasted the potential using three.js. He should have used it to create its own game engine and create games with it. Or using Godot engine for example. To make actual proper games that can be released commercially.

replies.author: syn_krown
replies.body:
Threejs is fully capable, and easy to turn into an executable app for all platforms(minus console, but who's making for console anyway?).

I always find building the game engine to fit the game better than using a general game engine...
